subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Triangles: Properties and Unknown Angles
seo_title: P5 Triangles Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths on Angles of a Triangle with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Properties of isosceles, equilateral and right-angled triangles; angle sum of a triangle; finding unknown angles
meta_desc: Free P5 maths practice: isosceles, equilateral and right-angled triangles, the 180° angle sum and unknown angles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The 3 angles of a triangle always add up to 180°.
key_sub: Two angles are 50° and 60°: the third angle is 180° − 50° − 60° = 70°.
body_html:
Types of triangles

Tick marks show equal sides. A small square shows a right angle (90°).

TriangleWhat to look forAngles
Isosceles2 equal sidesthe 2 base angles are equal
Equilateral3 equal sidesevery angle is 60°
Right-angled1 right anglethe other 2 angles add up to 90°

The angles add up to 180°

The 3 angles of every triangle add up to 180°, big or small. To find an unknown angle, subtract the two known angles from 180°.

Example 1

In triangle PQR, ∠P = 47° and ∠Q = 68°. Find ∠R.

47° + 68° = 115°. 180° − 115° = 65°.

Answer: ∠R = 65°

Isosceles triangles

The 2 equal sides meet at the top. The 2 angles at the ends of the third side (the base angles) are equal.

Example 2

In triangle XYZ, XY = XZ and ∠XYZ = 64°. Find ∠YXZ.

XY = XZ, so ∠XZY = 64° too. 180° − 64° − 64° = 52°.

Answer: ∠YXZ = 52°

Equilateral and right-angled triangles

An equilateral triangle has three 60° angles (180° ÷ 3). A right-angled triangle has exactly one right angle, so its other two angles add up to 90°.

Straight lines

Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. Use this first, then the angle sum of the triangle.

Example 3

In triangle ABC, ∠C = 80°. ∠A is 3 times the size of ∠B. Find ∠B.

∠A + ∠B = 180° − 80° = 100°. Draw a model: ∠A is 3 units and ∠B is 1 unit. 4 units = 100°, so 1 unit = 25°.

Answer: ∠B = 25°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Subtracting from 360°The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 360° is for four-sided figures
Subtracting only one known angleSubtract both known angles from 180°
Isosceles: forgetting to divide by 2180° − top angle, then ÷ 2 for each base angle
Isosceles: choosing the wrong equal anglesThe equal angles are at the ends of the side without tick marks
A right-angled triangle with 2 right anglesIt has exactly 1. The other 2 angles add up to 90°
Taking the angle outside the triangle as the one insideUse the straight line: 180° − outside angle

faq.q: What do P5 students learn about triangles?
faq.a: In Primary 5, students learn the properties of isosceles, equilateral and right-angled triangles, that the angles of a triangle add up to 180°, and how to find unknown angles in figures.

faq.q: How do I find the unknown angle in an isosceles triangle?
faq.a: The two base angles are equal. If you know the top angle, subtract it from 180° and divide by 2; if you know a base angle, subtract two base angles from 180°.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with angles of a triangle?
faq.a: Subtracting from 360° instead of 180°, or subtracting only one of the known angles. In isosceles triangles, many students forget to divide by 2.

faq.q: Is this topic in the MOE syllabus and the PSLE?
faq.a: Yes. Triangles and unknown angles are part of Geometry in the MOE Primary 5 syllabus, and unknown-angle questions in figures also appear in the PSLE at the end of Primary 6.

items.q: Which triangle is a right-angled triangle?
items.e: Triangle D has a small square in one corner, so one angle is 90°. It is turned, but it is still right-angled.

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?
items.e: Two sides are 6 cm, so exactly 2 sides are equal. The equal sides do not have to be the slanted ones.

items.q: Which triangle is an isosceles triangle?
items.e: Triangle B has tick marks on 2 sides, so it is isosceles, even though it points down. The other triangles have no equal sides.

items.q: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of 27 cm. How long is each side?
items.e: All 3 sides are equal: 27 ÷ 3 = 9 cm. (13.5 cm is 27 ÷ 2, and 81 cm is 27 × 3.)

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?
items.e: The small square marks a right angle (90°). No sides are equal, so it is a right-angled triangle. It is turned, but the small square still shows the right angle.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 8 cm, 8 cm and 5 cm. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: Two sides are 8 cm, so exactly 2 sides are equal. It is an isosceles triangle.

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?
items.e: All 3 sides have tick marks, so all 3 sides are equal. It is an equilateral triangle. Pointing down does not change its name.

items.q: An isosceles triangle has a perimeter of 20 cm. Its two equal sides are 7 cm each. How long is the third side?
items.e: 7 + 7 = 14 cm. 20 − 14 = 6 cm. (13 cm takes away only one of the 7 cm sides.)

items.q: Ethan says a triangle is isosceles only if it points up. Is he correct?
c: No, it can point any way
items.e: The name depends only on the sides. Turning an isosceles triangle does not change its 2 equal sides.

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?
items.e: Two sides have tick marks, so exactly 2 sides are equal. It has no right angle. It is an isosceles triangle. It lies on its side, but 2 sides still have tick marks. Turning a triangle never changes its name.

items.q: What do the tick marks on the sides of a triangle show?
items.e: Sides with the same tick marks have the same length. A small square, not a tick mark, shows a right angle.

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?
items.e: It has a right angle (the small square) and 2 equal sides (tick marks), so it is a right-angled isosceles triangle. It is turned, but the marks do not change.

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?
items.e: It has a right angle (the small square) and 2 equal sides (tick marks), so it is a right-angled isosceles triangle. The 2 equal sides are the arms of the right angle.

items.q: Hui Min says a right-angled triangle can also be an isosceles triangle. Is she correct?
c: No, it can only have one name
No, it must have 3 equal sides
items.e: A right-angled triangle with 2 equal sides is a right-angled isosceles triangle, like half of a square cut along a diagonal.

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?

items.q: Which triangle is an equilateral triangle?
items.e: Triangle A has tick marks on all 3 sides. The other triangles have only 2 equal sides.

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?
items.e: All 3 sides have tick marks, so all 3 sides are equal. It is an equilateral triangle. It is turned on its side, but all 3 sides are still equal.

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?
items.e: Two sides are 7.5 cm. It points down, but it is still isosceles.

items.q: Which is the best name for this triangle?
items.e: All 3 sides are 5 cm.

items.q: Find ∠x.
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 25° + 115° = 140°, and 180° − 140° = 40°. Subtract both known angles, not just one.

items.q: In triangle ABC, ∠A = 112° and ∠B = 29°. Find ∠C.
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 112° + 29° = 141°, and 180° − 141° = 39°.

items.q: In triangle XYZ, ∠X = 38° and ∠Z = 85°. Find ∠Y.
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 38° + 85° = 123°, and 180° − 123° = 57°.

items.q: Can a triangle have angles of 95° and 85°?
items.e: 95° + 85° = 180°. That leaves 0° for the third angle, so these cannot be two angles of a triangle.

items.q: Find ∠x.
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 45° + 105° = 150°, and 180° − 150° = 30°. Subtract both known angles, not just one.

items.q: Which set of angles can be the three angles of a triangle?
items.e: 35° + 65° + 80° = 180°, so these angles work. The others do not add up to 180°: 35°, 65°, 90° add up to 190°; 60°, 60°, 70° add up to 190°; 120°, 30°, 40° add up to 190°.

items.q: Ryan draws a big triangle and a small triangle. He says the angles of the big triangle add up to more. Is he correct?
c: No, the small one has more
items.e: The angles of every triangle add up to 180°, big or small. A bigger triangle has longer sides, not bigger angles.

items.q: Find ∠PRQ.
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 48° + 62° = 110°, and 180° − 110° = 70°.

items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 47° + 68° = 115°, and 180° − 115° = 65°.

items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 34° + 46° = 80°, and 180° − 80° = 100°.

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 26° and 19°. What is the third angle?
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 26° + 19° = 45°, and 180° − 45° = 135°.

items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 50° + 60° = 110°, and 180° − 110° = 70°. Subtract both known angles, not just one.

items.q: Chloe tears off the 3 corners of a paper triangle and puts them together, point to point. What do they make?
items.e: The 3 angles of a triangle add up to 180°, so the 3 corners fit together to make a straight line.

items.q: Which set of angles can be the three angles of a triangle?
items.e: 50° + 60° + 70° = 180°, so these angles work. The others do not add up to 180°: 50°, 60°, 80° add up to 190°; 90°, 45°, 55° add up to 190°; 100°, 50°, 40° add up to 190°.

items.q: Find ∠DEF.
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 57° + 52° = 109°, and 180° − 109° = 71°.

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 73° and 54°. What is the third angle?
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 73° + 54° = 127°, and 180° − 127° = 53°.

items.q: The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 equal sides, so the 2 angles at the ends of the third side are equal. 180° − 110° = 70°, and 70° ÷ 2 = 35°. (70° forgets to divide by 2.)

The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 equal sides, so the 2 angles at the ends of the third side are equal. 180° − 36° = 144°, and 144° ÷ 2 = 72°. (144° forgets to divide by 2.)

items.q: The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The tick marks show the 2 equal sides. The angles opposite them, at the ends of the third side, are equal. So ∠x = 64°. (52° is the angle at the top.)

items.q: The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The 2 base angles are equal, so the other base angle is also 35°. 180° − 35° − 35° = 110°. (145° subtracts only one base angle.)

items.q: The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 equal sides, so the 2 angles at the ends of the third side are equal. 180° − 40° = 140°, and 140° ÷ 2 = 70°. (140° forgets to divide by 2.)

items.q: In triangle XYZ, XY = XZ and ∠XYZ = 64°. Find ∠YXZ.
items.e: XY = XZ, so ∠XZY = ∠XYZ = 64°. 180° − 64° − 64° = 52°. (116° subtracts only one 64° angle.)

items.q: Each base angle of an isosceles triangle is 45°. Find the angle at the top.
items.e: 180° − 45° − 45° = 90°. So it is a right-angled isosceles triangle. (135° subtracts only one 45° angle.)

items.q: Which set of angles can be the three angles of an isosceles triangle?
items.e: 110° + 35° + 35° = 180°, and two angles are equal. The others add up to 190°, 170° and 190°.

items.q: The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The 2 base angles are equal, so the other base angle is also 70°. 180° − 70° − 70° = 40°. (110° subtracts only one base angle.)

items.q: In an isosceles triangle, the angle at the top is 3 times the size of each base angle. Find a base angle.
items.e: Base + base + top = 1 unit + 1 unit + 3 units = 5 units = 180°. 1 unit = 180° ÷ 5 = 36°. (The top angle is 108°.)

items.q: The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The 2 base angles are equal, so the other base angle is also 38°. 180° − 38° − 38° = 104°. (142° subtracts only one base angle.)

items.q: One angle of an isosceles triangle is 100°. Find each of the other two angles.
items.e: Two angles of 100° would add up to more than 180°, so 100° is the angle at the top. 180° − 100° = 80°, and 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.

items.q: In triangle PQR, PQ = PR. Which two angles are equal?
items.e: The equal sides PQ and PR meet at P. The 2 equal angles are at the other two corners, Q and R: ∠PQR and ∠PRQ.

items.q: The two equal angles of an isosceles triangle add up to 130°. What is the third angle?
items.e: 180° − 130° = 50°. (65° is each equal angle, not the third angle.)

items.q: The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The 2 base angles are equal, so the other base angle is also 52°. 180° − 52° − 52° = 76°. (128° subtracts only one base angle.)

items.q: The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The tick marks show 2 equal sides, so the 2 angles at the ends of the third side are equal. 180° − 50° = 130°, and 130° ÷ 2 = 65°. (130° forgets to divide by 2.)

items.q: In triangle XYZ, XY = XZ. Which two angles are equal?
items.e: The equal sides XY and XZ meet at X. The 2 equal angles are at the other two corners, Y and Z: ∠XYZ and ∠XZY.

items.q: In triangle DEF, DE = DF and ∠EDF = 90°. Find ∠DEF.
items.e: DE = DF, so ∠DEF = ∠DFE. 180° − 90° = 90°, and 90° ÷ 2 = 45°. (90° forgets to divide by 2.)

items.q: The triangle is an isosceles triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: The tick marks show the 2 equal sides. The angles opposite them, at the ends of the third side, are equal. So ∠x = 28°. (124° is the angle at the top.)

items.q: What is the size of each angle of an equilateral triangle?
items.e: The 3 angles are equal and add up to 180°: 180° ÷ 3 = 60°. (120° comes from 360° ÷ 3.)

items.q: An equilateral triangle has sides of 12 cm. What is the size of each angle?
items.e: Every equilateral triangle has three 60° angles (180° ÷ 3), whatever the length of its sides. (12° mixes up the side length with the angle, and 36° is the perimeter.)

items.q: The triangle is an equilateral triangle. Find its perimeter.
items.e: All 3 sides are 7 cm. 3 × 7 = 21 cm. (14 cm counts only 2 sides.)

items.q: Kumar says a triangle with angles of 60°, 60° and 60° must have 3 equal sides. Is he correct?
c: Yes, but only if it is small
items.e: Equal angles go with equal sides. A triangle with three 60° angles is an equilateral triangle, whatever its size.

items.q: Can a triangle have one right angle and one angle of 100°?
c: No, they add up to over 180°
items.e: 90° + 100° = 190°, which is already more than 180°.

items.q: Ali draws a right-angled triangle. He says it has a right angle at each end of the base. Is he correct?
items.e: 90° + 90° = 180° leaves nothing for the third angle. A right-angled triangle has exactly 1 right angle.

items.q: The triangle is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: All 3 sides are equal, so all 3 angles are equal. 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.

items.q: What is the greatest number of right angles a triangle can have?
items.e: Two right angles already make 90° + 90° = 180°. That leaves 0° for the third angle, so a triangle has at most 1 right angle.

items.q: Find ∠x.
items.e: The small square is a right angle, 90°. 180° − 90° − 38° = 52°. (142° forgets the right angle.)

items.q: The triangle is an equilateral triangle. Find ∠x.
items.e: All 3 sides are equal, so all 3 angles are equal. 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.

Find ∠x.
items.e: The small square is a right angle, 90°. 180° − 90° − 61° = 29°. (119° forgets the right angle.)

items.q: Find ∠x.
items.e: The small square is a right angle, 90°. 180° − 90° − 27° = 63°. (153° forgets the right angle.)

items.q: Find ∠x.
items.e: The small square is a right angle, 90°. 180° − 90° − 34° = 56°. (146° forgets the right angle.)

items.q: Find ∠PRQ.
items.e: ∠QPR is a right angle (90°). ∠PRQ = 180° − 90° − 40° = 50°. (140° forgets the right angle.)

items.q: Find ∠x.
items.e: It is a right-angled isosceles triangle, so the other 2 angles are equal. 180° − 90° = 90°, and 90° ÷ 2 = 45°.

items.q: In triangle ABC, ∠ABC = 90° and ∠BAC = 38°. Find ∠ACB.
items.e: 180° − 90° − 38° = 52°. (142° forgets the right angle.)

items.q: In a right-angled triangle, one acute angle is 2 times the size of the other acute angle. Find the smaller acute angle.
items.e: The two angles add up to 90°. 2 units + 1 unit = 3 units = 90°, so 1 unit = 90° ÷ 3 = 30°. (60° is the larger angle.)

items.q: Siti folds a square piece of paper along a diagonal. What triangle does she get?
c: right-angled triangle with no equal sides
isosceles triangle with no right angle
items.e: The corner of the square is 90°, and two sides of the square are equal. So it is a right-angled isosceles triangle (angles 90°, 45°, 45°).

items.q: The two angles of a right-angled triangle that are not right angles add up to
items.e: All 3 angles add up to 180°, and the right angle takes 90°. 180° − 90° = 90° is left for the other two.

items.e: In triangle ADC: ∠x = 180° − 80° − 65° = 35°. (50° is the whole ∠BAC.)

items.q: The roof of a sheltered walkway near a void deck is an isosceles triangle. The angle at the top is 120°. Find each of the other two angles.
items.e: 180° − 120° = 60°, shared by 2 equal angles: 60° ÷ 2 = 30°. (60° forgets to divide by 2.)
